title: Residue-field tests determine lowest fibre ranks
statement: Let $S,T$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], with derived categories in one universe [def-pc-derived-category], and $E\in D(\mathcal O_S)$ perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex]. Let $a,b\in\mathbf Z$, and assume $H^i(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}F)=0$ for every module sheaf $F$ and every $i<a$ or $b<i$ [def-pc-derived-tensor-cohomology-vanishes]. Fix $h:T\to S$, $r\in\mathbf N$, and suppose $H^a(L(h\circ i_t)^*E)$ is finite locally free of rank $r$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module] for every residue morphism $i_t:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)\to T$ [def-pc-derived-pullback]. Then at every $t\in T$, $\beta_i(E,h(t))=0$ for all $i<a$ and $\beta_a(E,h(t))=r$ [def-sc-derived-fiber-betti]. No condition $a\le b$ is assumed.

source.place: First paragraph; Tag 0BDI base-change formula, Tag 09U8 Tor amplitude under pullback, Tag 08E9 affine criterion

proof.text: Unpack each K-flat witness of schemeDerivedTensorCohomologyVanishes. Use the K-flat derived tensor comparison, the singleFunctorIsoCompQ isomorphism, and homologyFunctorFactors to obtain zero homology of E tensor F[0]. By the two t-structure characterizations this is categorical Tor amplitude in [a,b]. The category of structure-sheaf modules has its recorded symmetric closed tensor, Grothendieck structure and functorial flat resolutions. Apply the existing general source flat-model theorem to obtain P representing E, flat and strictly supported in [a,b]; it does not require a <= b.

At h(t), apply flatComplexDerivedPullback to P along the residue morphism. Compose the canonical quotientCompQhIso and mapHomotopyCategoryFactors comparisons with Q(P) ≅ E to identify the derived residue pullback with Q of the termwise pullback Q. For i<a, P.X i is zero, hence Q.X i and Q.homology i are zero. homologyFunctorFactors transports this to zero derived homology. Evaluation and restriction of scalars preserve zero objects, giving zero derivedFiberCohomology. ModuleCat.subsingleton_of_isZero and Module.finrank_zero_of_subsingleton yield the required zero Betti number.

Use exists_derivedPullbackComposition at the residue morphism of t and h; its degree-a homology isomorphism transports hres(t) to a rank-r finite locally free sheaf representing the fibre cohomology of Lh*E. On Spec kappa(t), choose a point and a member of the trivializing open cover containing it. Every point equals this point, so that open is top. isoFreeOfRestrictIso gives a global free-sheaf isomorphism. The proved finrank_moduleSpecΓFunctor_obj_free gives finrank r, including r=0.

Apply derivedFiberCohomology_baseChange_iso to E, h, a, and t. Its ModuleCat isomorphism preserves finrank. With the algebra structure induced by h.residueFieldMap t, Module.finrank_baseChange says extension of fields preserves the original finrank, without a finiteness hypothesis. Thus the Betti number of Lh*E at t equals that of E at h(t). Combine this equality with the rank-r sections calculation and the zero Betti numbers proved above. The perfectness hypothesis is unused; the original interface is unchanged.

lean.statement:
theorem universalLowest_fiber_ranks
    [∀ Y : Scheme.{u}, HasDerivedCategory.{w}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    (S : Scheme.{u})
    [∀ U : S.Opens, HasDerivedCategory.{w}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings S.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (E : schemeDerivedCategory S) (hE : IsPerfect S E) (a b : ℤ)
    (hamp : ∀ F : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings S.toRingedSpace),
      ∀ i : ℤ, i < a ∨ b < i → schemeDerivedTensorCohomologyVanishes S E F i)
    (r : ℕ) (T : Scheme.{u}) (h : T ⟶ S)
    (hres : ∀ t : T,
      SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfRank.{u, u, u}
        ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor
          (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (Spec (T.residueField t)).toRingedSpace)) a).obj
            ((derivedPullback (T.fromSpecResidueField t ≫ h)).obj E)) r) :
    ∀ t : T, (∀ i : ℤ, i < a → derivedFiberBetti S E i (h t) = 0) ∧
      derivedFiberBetti S E a (h t) = r
